intro: I am a development economist and management-consulting leader. I work across economic appraisal, policy research and programme delivery, helping teams turn complex evidence into choices they can assess and implement.
scope: My career spans agriculture, public health, industry, infrastructure, trade and public finance. I have contributed to more than 100 government- and international development partner-funded programmes across public and private sectors.

metrics.label: World Bank South Asia experience
metrics.detail: Economist (STC) and analytical and operational assignments associated with SARCE.

worldBank.summary: For five years, I worked as an Economist (STC) and contributed to analytical and operational assignments associated with the Office of the Chief Economist for South Asia (SARCE) at the World Bank. This included research needs from economists in Finance, Competitiveness and Innovation (FCI), Equity, Growth and Institutions (EFI), and requests from other departments.
worldBank.delivery: I supported World Bank-commissioned research and surveys in Bangladesh from early design through budgeting, research inputs, implementation, coordination, analysis and dissemination. The work meant balancing requests across teams and coordinating with economists, research firms, specialists and local partners.
worldBank.leadership: Across assignments, I have assembled firms and professional teams, coordinated researchers and implementers, and contributed to programme design, delivery, monitoring, evaluation and scale-up. My focus is clear scope, sound evidence and work that fits the institutional context.
